producer_to_boundary_trace: The personal and party native database tables independently auto-allocate u64 primary keys. add_inventory_item_checked returns Option<u64> and passes item.id to personal object and food initialization; party creation likewise passes party row.id to its object and food initialization.

InventoryLocation identifies personal versus party in its enum variant but retains each backing row as u64. object_for_row and ensure_food_material_object accept an independently supplied CarriedInventoryScope and u64, select a table by the scope, and compare numeric row IDs. FoodLot persists separate optional numeric fields for the two table references.

Storefront reducer ABI supplies Vec<u64> and a scope bool to StorefrontTradeRequest::parse. Parsing checks line alignment and positive quantities, but retains each sale ID as u64 and scope as a separate public enum field. The private executor converts that enum back to a bool, extracts vectors, selects the corresponding lookup and table, and applies sales using the same separated values. The selected source does check row ownership and duplicate sale IDs; no incorrect sale is asserted.

The character creator InventoryItemId belongs to an in-memory character-creator article collection with its own per-collection allocation, rather than the shown persisted strategic personal or party tables. Its similar spelling does not establish shared identity or a safe existing owner for those row IDs.
first_contract: At native row creation or reducer decoding, personal and party identifiers lose their table distinction in application APIs and retained request state; callers must keep the separate scope paired correctly. Determine the shared owner and carry identity through each connected internal producer, field, operation and consumer until an actual database or transport adapter requires a primitive.
